title: Claims paid, and how much of that the Board voted on
question: How much does the City pay out on claims and judgments each year, and how much of it comes before the Board as a settlement?
finding: The City’s financial report shows claim payments of $70.1 million in fiscal 2019 and $201.5 million in fiscal 2025, $767.8 million over the seven years. Settlements the Board passed in those years in which the City pays name $238.5 million, 31% of that. Until October 2026 the City Attorney could settle up to $25,000 without the Board; ordinance 205-26, passed on 2 October 2026, raised that to $100,000 with a yearly report in place of a vote. 228 of the 502 settlements the Board passed since fiscal 2019 (45%) were at or under $100,000, $13.6 million in all: files of that size will no longer come to the Board. By subject the files are injury or property damage (263); other (99); employment (97); civil rights (43). 2 further files since fiscal 2015 gave a department and the City Attorney standing authority to settle every claim from one event (a landslide, a pipeline break) up to a ceiling, $12.0 million between them.
how: Claim payments and year-end liability are from the risk-management note of each Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (the table of changes in estimated claims payable; thousands of dollars as printed). The ledger column is the Controller’s Spending and Revenue table, account “Judgments & Claims”. Board files are those titled as settlements and passed, with the dollar figure in the title, counted in the fiscal year passed, leaving out settlements in which the City is paid and settlements of tax-refund claims (shown in their own screen). The delegation limits are read from the title of the ordinance that changed them. Parties to settlements are not listed.
limits: The two totals are not the same thing, so the share is a rough gauge and not a count of unvoted money. The report’s claim payments cover every fund and include health-benefit claims paid directly to providers; a settlement can be paid in a later year than the vote, in instalments, or from insurance; and court judgments are paid without any settlement file. Delegating small settlements is ordinary practice and the new ordinance requires an annual report of those between the old and new limits. The fiscal 2025 report says the City changed how it estimates the amount owed at year end, so that column is not comparable with earlier years. The title search may miss settlements filed under another heading. What would settle it: the City Attorney’s annual claims report, which is not among the documents on disk. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
